decisions.executionNote: Begin elbow-up approach to the rear-left tube, raising the wrist while pitching the open gripper downward; right arm stays parked.
Continue the elbow-up arc toward the rear-left tube and align the open jaws with its axis. Approach remains above the table.
Fine-align over the rear-left tube using the wrist view and lower to a tentative grasp height with jaws open.
Correct the wrist-view lateral and axial offset without further descending; tube is not yet centered between the jaws.
Make a small axial correction and close the left gripper around the tube body; retention will be checked on lifting.
Lift the closed left gripper clear of the table with a slight retreat; check whether the first tube follows securely.
The tube follows the left gripper. Begin rotating it upright and moving toward a left-side rack slot while keeping it elevated.
Finish rotating the retained tube upright above the left rack slot; maintain clearance before insertion.
Visually correct the tube over the front-left large opening and descend partway, keeping the gripper closed.
Resubmit corrected stationary-right-arm tensor; approach the front-left opening slowly with the tube retained.
The tube tip appears at the opening but has tilted on contact. Make a minimal vertical seating motion, then release to let it settle and inspect.
Withdraw the open left gripper upward and back to expose the first tube and rack; seating is uncertain after release.
The first tube is not upright, so clear the left arm for later recovery. Begin a separate elbow-up approach to the right-hand tube.
Approach the right tube from above with open jaws, aligning its diagonal axis. Return the empty left arm toward its origin without crossing workspaces.
Lower the right wrist toward a centered body grasp, completing the downward orientation. Keep the left arm parked open.
Center the right tube body between the jaws with a small forward-left correction, then close before lifting.
Lift the closed right gripper to verify retention and clear the table before turning the tube upright.
The right tube is retained. Rotate it toward upright above the right side of the rack, preserving a high, elbow-up approach.
Continue the gradual upright rotation and right-slot approach with the tube held clear of the rack.
Finish bringing the retained right tube upright and position above a right-side large slot before a cautious vertical descent.
Correct toward the right-front large opening using the calibrated head view, then lower partway while checking tube alignment.
Lower the upright right tube slowly into the aligned opening, watching for any rotation or contact-induced displacement.
The right tube remains upright at the opening but has begun sliding in the jaws. Stop downward motion, release gently, and withdraw a little to inspect seating.
Clear the right gripper fully from the rack and allow the released tube to settle; its tilt makes successful insertion uncertain.
The right tube has settled upright in its slot. Park the empty right arm and begin the left-arm approach to the remaining loose diagonal tube.
Continue toward the loose left tube while aligning the open jaws with its diagonal axis; finish parking the right arm.
Complete the downward approach to the diagonal tube, then use the wrist view to refine centering before grasping.
The loose tube rotated during approach. Reorient the open left gripper along its newly observed axis and refine centering without descending further.
Lift the open jaws clear before further alignment so they do not roll the tube. Adjust yaw and lateral position to its current nearly horizontal axis.
The loose tube is now centered and aligned. Approach the body just below its cap while maintaining the open-jaw alignment.
Refine the centered body grasp just below the cap, then close the left gripper without moving the tube along the table.
Lift the newly grasped left tube clear of the table and the leaning tube before rotating it toward the empty middle slot.
The tube follows the left gripper. Begin a gradual upright rotation above the table toward the empty middle rack slot.
Continue turning the retained tube upright while moving toward the middle opening, maintaining clearance over the rack.
Finish orienting the tube upright over the middle front opening; stay high for a visual alignment check before descending.
Lower the upright left-held tube over the middle opening, with a small lateral correction and without disturbing the seated right tube.
Descend slowly into the middle slot with the tube upright and jaws closed; monitor for sliding or tilting before release.
The middle tube is upright but has started sliding on contact. Stop pressing, open the jaws, and withdraw slightly to let it settle in the slot.
Clear the middle tube to let it settle, then prepare to recover the first tube leaning against the front-left of the rack.
The middle tube fell forward and will also need recovery. Reorient the open left gripper above the leaning first tube, matching its cap-forward direction.
Continue the high, open-jaw recovery approach to the left leaning tube, preserving elbow-up continuity.
Bring the open left gripper closer above the leaning tube while completing the cap-forward recovery orientation.
Complete the open-jaw orientation along the leaning tube and approach from above for a wrist-view grasp alignment check.
Use the wrist view to center the first leaning tube between the open jaws, with a shallow approach and small axis correction.
Refine the leaning tube's axis and body centering, then close the left jaws for a cautious recovery lift.
Lift the recovered tube away from the rack and the remaining loose tube, retaining it with the closed left gripper.
The recovered tube is retained. Begin a slow continuous rotation toward upright while keeping it above and clear of the rack.
Continue the retained tube's upright rotation above the left rack area; the grasped tube's residual tilt will need correction before insertion.
Continue rotating the recovered tube at fixed height, keeping it clear while its tip turns downward.
Finish the main upright rotation at fixed clearance height, then inspect the recovered tube's actual axis before descending.
